payload.title: plan_write_scope.DRIFT_CLASS_SIDES lists only enum_drift and ui_option_drift while the seeder now mints a third class, and the test that claims every minted class is in the table builds its fixture without a graphql section, so it cannot see the gap.
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/plan_write_scope.py:74-82 (the table and the copy-side map, three classes minted, two listed)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/plan_write_scope.py:137-151 (_copy_index indexes DRIFT_CLASS_SIDES[str(drift_class)] after the copy-side lookup)
aria-kernel/tests/test_plan_write_scope.py:152-172 (asserts set(DRIFT_CLASS_SIDES) equals the classes written, fixture has no graphql_operations section)
payload.rule_violated: A pin must fail when the thing it names changes: the comment 'Every class the seeder mints has its sides in the table' is not enforced for the third class.
payload.notes: graphql_drifts returns [] for the fixture document, so select_candidates never mints the third class and the equality assertion stays green. Today the class is safe because DRIFT_COPY_SIDES has no entry and _copy_index returns before the table lookup; the day a copy side is declared for graphql_operation_drift, DRIFT_CLASS_SIDES[...] raises KeyError inside plan admission with every test still green. Close condition: Add graphql_operation_drift with sides ('ui', 'source') to the table and add a graphql_operations section with one drift to the fixture so the existing equality assertion covers the class; better, derive the class set from one constant exported by the seeder that both sides read.
